worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{t}-(-{e}^{t})\cdot 2{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & {e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & {e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=\frac{4}{3}t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=\frac{4}{3}\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{4}{3}t\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}\cdot (\frac{4}{3}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}t{e}^{2t}-\frac{2}{3}\int {e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{2}{3}t{e}^{2t}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t}(2t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=-\frac{8}{3}t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-\frac{8}{3}\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-{e}^{-t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t & =-\frac{8}{3}t\cdot (-{e}^{-t})-\int -{e}^{-t}\cdot (-\frac{8}{3}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}-\frac{8}{3}\int {e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}+\frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t}(t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t}(2t-1) \\ \frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t}(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}(2t-1)-8(t+1) \\ 2(2t-1)+8(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2t-3 \\ 4t+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Φ−1f(t)=13[e2te2t−2e−te−t][4t0]=[43te2t−83te−t].

  • For the second component, let u=−83t and dv=e−tdt. Then, du=−83dt and v=−e−t. So, ∫−83te−tdt=−83t⋅(−e−t)−∫−e−t⋅(−83dt)=83te−t−83∫e−tdt=83te−t+83e−t=83e−t(t+1).
